newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says to sign Brady exchange agreement Friday.
newsitem.headline: Peru says to sign Brady exchange agreement Friday.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Tuesday it would sign with its creditor banks in Toronto on Friday a Brady bond exchange agreement outlining the final details of its $10.657 billion commercial debt restructuring deal.
Economy Ministry officials said the formal closing of the Brady Plan, which will include a buyback and an exchange of debt for bonds, was scheduled for December 20.
"What we are going to sign in Toronto is the master copy for the issuance of the bonds," a senior government official told Reuters.
The Brady restructuring accord will reduce total commercial debt to around $5 billion, according to the government.

The official, who asked not to be named, said 30 percent of this would be covered by a debt buyback. The banks have made selections that would convert a further 50 percent to Front Loaded Interest Rate Bonds (FLIRBs), 15 percent to Discount bonds, and five percent to par bonds.
"However, we want to reduce the FLIRBs to 40 percent or less, which would mean increasing the Discounts to 25 percent or more," the official added.
He said the precise financing of the Brady deal, and the "reconciliation" of some interest, or agreement with bank creditors on exactly how much interest is owed, had still not been finalized.
"But we will be able to close even if we have not finished this process. This can continue afterwards," he added.
